meta.title: Industrial Music Knowledge Graph
meta.scope: A deliberately small, evidence-ready seed graph. Inclusion is not a claim of exhaustive membership or discography.
meta.temporalPolicy: validFrom and validTo describe when a node or relationship is known to apply; absent values mean not yet researched.

nodes.label: Ministry
nodes.summary: American industrial project founded by Al Jourgensen.

nodes.label: Skinny Puppy
nodes.summary: Canadian industrial group centered on cEvin Key and Nivek Ogre.

nodes.label: Front 242
nodes.summary: Belgian electronic body music group.

nodes.label: Front Line Assembly
nodes.summary: Canadian industrial project founded by Bill Leeb.

nodes.label: KMFDM
nodes.summary: German-founded industrial rock group.

nodes.label: Revolting Cocks
nodes.summary: Industrial supergroup with Ministry and Front 242 connections.

nodes.label: Al Jourgensen
nodes.summary: Musician and producer; founder of Ministry.

nodes.label: Paul Barker
nodes.summary: Musician and producer associated with Ministry.

nodes.label: cEvin Key
nodes.summary: Musician and co-founder of Skinny Puppy.

nodes.label: Nivek Ogre
nodes.summary: Vocalist and co-founder of Skinny Puppy.

nodes.label: Bill Leeb
nodes.summary: Musician; founder of Front Line Assembly.

nodes.label: Rhys Fulber
nodes.summary: Composer and producer associated with Front Line Assembly.

nodes.label: Sascha Konietzko
nodes.summary: Musician and founder of KMFDM.

nodes.label: Richard 23
nodes.summary: Musician associated with Front 242 and Revolting Cocks.

nodes.label: The Land of Rape and Honey

nodes.label: Tactical Neural Implant

nodes.label: 1000 Homo DJs
nodes.summary: Industrial side project documented through its recordings of Supernaut.

nodes.label: Trent Reznor
nodes.summary: Contextual collaborator: vocalist on the Trent Reznor vocal version of 1000 Homo DJs' Supernaut.

nodes.label: Supernaut
nodes.summary: 1000 Homo DJs recording of the Black Sabbath song, documented with distinct Al Jourgensen and Trent Reznor vocal versions.
